## A. Over-long code comments that re-type the design record (AGENTS.md breach)

The rule: *"If an explanation needs a paragraph, it belongs in `docs/design-decisions/` with at most a one-line pointer from the code. A comment that repeats the design record is a second copy to keep in sync, and it will drift."* The existing repo precedent is `frontend/src/api/queryKeys.ts`, whose docstring ends `See docs/design-decisions/36-sse-event-module.md.` — match that shape.

Note the rule's own limit: TSDoc stating **intent** on a type or non-trivial function is explicitly welcome, and a one-line warning *"where the obvious edit is the wrong one"* is explicitly permitted. So do not strip these to nothing — reduce each to the intent plus the genuinely non-obvious *why*, and move the argument to the pointer. `frontend/README.md` and `docs/design-decisions/38-accounts-list-screen.md` already carry the full statement and the reasoning respectively; **do not edit either of them** — they are the copies that are supposed to survive.

1. **`frontend/e2e/harness/focus.ts`** — worst case, and it has a real bug: the file opens with a `/** … */` block of ~17 lines that is immediately followed by `setVisibility`'s own `/** … */`. TSDoc attaches only the second, so that first block documents nothing at all. Delete or fold it. Keep, on each of the two exports, a short docstring saying what it is for and the one or two facts a reader cannot get from the code — that the event goes to `window` because that is where the focus manager listens, and that the state must move before the dispatch because `isFocused()` reads `document.visibilityState` when the event arrives. Move the Chromium-removed-`Emulation.setPageVisibilityState` history and the `page.evaluate`-doesn't-survive-navigation paragraph behind `See docs/design-decisions/38-accounts-list-screen.md.` — **except** keep the navigation limitation as a one-line warning if you can state it in one line, because it is exactly the "obvious edit is the wrong one" case (a spec that navigates between the two halves silently tests nothing).
2. **`frontend/e2e/accounts/accounts.spec.ts`** — same shape at the top of the file (a floating block comment attached to nothing). Reduce it. Also review the per-test doc comments in that file: keep the ones stating a non-obvious why (the HUF row's purpose; why there is no `goto` between the two halves of the focus test), trim any that narrate what the code does.
3. **`frontend/src/api/accounts.ts`** — the docstring's third paragraph is the design record's paragraph verbatim. Reduce the `throw`-the-parsed-body explanation to one sentence naming the two downstream readers, plus the pointer.
4. **`frontend/src/api/queryClient.ts`** — two comment blocks. **Keep the `staleTime` one**, tightened to one or two lines: it is a warning where the obvious edit is wrong, which AGENTS.md permits. Reduce the `refetchOnWindowFocus` one to a short why plus the pointer.
5. **`frontend/src/routes/accounts.module.css`** — delete the comment. `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` restates itself, and AGENTS.md's configuration-file exception covers `application.properties`-style keys, not CSS. (Keep the rule itself.)

Also check `frontend/src/routes/accounts.tsx`'s docstrings against the same rule and trim any paragraph that re-argues the record — but its component docstrings looked proportionate, so change little.

## B. Two small code fixes

6. **`frontend/src/api/accounts.test.ts`** — a module-level `let requestedPath` is written by every stubbed call and never reset, while the surrounding `answering` helper otherwise restores state carefully in a `finally`. Make the recorded path scoped to the call that reads it (e.g. have the helper return it, or reset it) so a later test cannot read a stale value. Also make it obvious at the call site that `answering(...)` stubs `globalThis.fetch` — rename it if a clearly better name exists, otherwise a one-line docstring.
7. **`frontend/src/routes/accounts.tsx`, `AccountRow`** — it destructures `{ id, currency }` from `account` and then reaches for `account.balanceMinorUnits` directly. Pick one style and apply it consistently.

## C. Two missing assertions in the browser spec (the Spec axis's real findings)

Both go in `frontend/e2e/accounts/accounts.spec.ts`.

8. **Row order is contract and nothing asserts it.** `GET /api/accounts` returns Accounts oldest-first and *"the order is part of the listing's contract rather than a detail of the query"* — nothing in the frontend may sort. Today's fixture uses ids 1 then 2 in ascending order, so even a client-side sort-by-id would pass. Fix by scripting Accounts whose received order is **not** their id order (e.g. id 2 first, then id 1) and asserting the rendered `tbody` row order matches the order the API sent. No fixed timeouts — web-first assertions only.

9. **"The Available Balance is rendered, never computed" has no test that can fail.** The `anAccount` fixture *derives* `availableBalanceMinorUnits = balance − reserved`, so every current assertion passes equally against a screen that subtracts client-side. A short doc comment should say why an impossible Account is the only way to tell the two implementations apart.

`npm test`, `npx tsc -b --force`, `npx oxlint`, `npm run test:browser`. Then run `npx playwright test e2e/accounts/accounts.spec.ts` **3 consecutive times** — `retries: 0` is load-bearing and the new order/impossible-Account tests must not be flaky.

Exit codes for every gate, the consecutive-run evidence, the final content of `focus.ts` and of the two new/changed tests in `accounts.spec.ts`, and a one-line note per numbered finding saying what you did (or, if you concluded a fix was wrong, say so and why rather than silently skipping it).

content.text:
Ticket 38 is done and committed on `worktree-ticket-38-accounts-list` (one commit, `f27cd39`, ahead of `master`).

## What shipped

**The screen** — `frontend/src/routes/accounts.tsx` renders a Bootstrap table: Account, Currency, Balance, Reserved Amount, Available Balance. The Currency is a column rather than a suffix on three numbers, because an Account is denominated once. Reserved Amount is there beyond the two required figures, since the ticket's prose asks that an operator see "how much of an Account is already committed to in-flight Transfers".

**Data** — `frontend/src/api/accounts.ts` (`listAccounts`, TDD'd first) throws the parsed problem body rather than an `Error`, which is what `problem.ts` and `retry.ts` are both written to read. Filed under `queryKeys.accounts()`, so ticket 42's invalidation reaches it for free.

**States** — spinner, an empty message instead of a headless table, and an error rendered through `problemToMessage`, with a *Try again* button driven by its `retryable` rather than by the retry rule.

**Focus refetch** — `refetchOnWindowFocus: true` is now declared rather than inherited. The load-bearing half is the *absent* `staleTime`: a focus only refetches what is already stale, so any non-zero value would defeat it while leaving the declaration looking correct.

## The one thing worth your attention

Making a real focus happen in headless Chromium cost a spike. `Emulation.setPageVisibilityState` has been removed, and a backgrounded page still reports `visible` — `newPage()` + `bringToFront()` fires no `visibilitychange` and the refetch simply never happens. The new `e2e/harness/focus.ts` redefines `document.visibilityState` and dispatches on `window` (where TanStack's focus manager listens), moving the state *before* the dispatch. Splitting it into `setVisibility` and `refocus` is what lets the spec assert the negative — a tab that stayed away must not refetch. Ticket 43 will want the same helper.

## Review found two real gaps, both now closed

Nothing asserted **row order** (the fixture used ascending ids, so a client-side sort would have passed), and nothing could distinguish the server's **Available Balance** from a client subtraction (the `anAccount` fixture derives it). Both are now pinned by specs — the second using an Account the backend could never produce.

**Gates:** 91 unit tests, 12 browser specs, `tsc -b` and `oxlint` all clean; the accounts spec ran 3× consecutively with `retries: 0`, no flake.

**Disclosed, not dropped:** the loading state is rendered but not asserted — the harness answers every request immediately and has no way to hold one. That's in `docs/deferred.md` with the note that fixing it is a ticket-37 harness change.

Want me to land this onto `master` and remove the worktree?
